region: Throughout settled lowland and mid-altitude areas nationwide (introduced in prehistoric times)
treatment_methods: Borax-boric acid (BBA) soak / vertical soak diffusion
description: The Philippines' most important structural bamboo — thorny, thick-walled, and high-density, widely used for posts, framing, and engineered bamboo. Three- to four-year-old culms show high relative density, compressive strength, and modulus of elasticity suitable for low-rise housing. Figures vary with age, site, and moisture content.
sources: BioResources — Determining material suitability for low-rise housing in the Philippines: physical and mechanical properties of Bambusa blumeana: https://bioresources.cnr.ncsu.edu/resources/determining-material-suitability-for-low-rise-housing-in-the-philippines-physical-and-mechanical-properties-of-the-bamboo-species-bambusa-blumeana/
Base Bahay Foundation / DLSU — Establishing the Characteristic Shear Strength of Bambusa blumeana (Kawayan Tinik): https://base-builds.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/SEE-15.pdf

region: Cultivated nationwide (introduced); notable plantations in Bukidnon, Mindanao
density: Green specific gravity site-dependent, ≈0.5-0.7 (upland culms denser than riparian)
treatment_methods: Borax-boric acid (BBA) soak / vertical soak diffusion
description: Large-diameter, thick-walled species favored for engineered bamboo and heavy structural members. Philippine studies (Bukidnon) found culm diameter, wall thickness, density and bending strength all site-dependent, with mid-elevation and upland culms performing best.
sources: Site influence on the morphological, physical and mechanical properties of giant bamboo (Dendrocalamus asper) in Bukidnon, Mindanao: https://www.ukdr.uplb.edu.ph/journal-articles/872/

Base Bahay — Establishing the Strength Parameters Parallel to Fiber of Dendrocalamus asper: https://base-builds.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Establishing-the-Strength-Parameters-Parallel-to-Fiber-of-Dendrocalamus-Asper-Giant-Bamboo.pdf

region: Cultivated across the Philippines (locally naturalized); also Borneo
density: Specific gravity 0.5-0.6 (≈500-600 kg/m³); green moisture content 94-143%
wall_thickness_range: Thin-walled (culm-wall value site-dependent; species-specific figure not openly published)
treatment_methods: Borax-boric acid (BBA) soak / vertical soak diffusion
description: Straight, relatively smooth, thin-walled culms used for light framing, flooring slats, and walling. Culm wall thickness, diameter, specific gravity, MOE and MOR are all reported as location-dependent. Culm-wall thickness figure is approximate pending a species-specific test value.

density: Specific gravity ≈0.45 (≈450 kg/m³); moisture content ~112-115% green
culm_diam_range: 80-120 mm (a Capiz study measured mean Ø 65.8 mm)
treatment_methods: Borax-boric acid (BBA) soak / vertical soak diffusion
description: An endemic Philippine species valued for its strength and thick, strong culms — traditionally used in house construction, furniture, fishpond and boat building, and as tying material. A study of plantation culms (Dumarao, Capiz) reported mean modulus of elasticity ≈3.94 GPa and modulus of rupture ≈138.9 MPa. Taxonomy is unsettled between Dendrocalamus merrillianus and Bambusa merrilliana.
sources: Rojo & Roxas — Physico-Mechanical Properties of Culturally-Preformed Bayog (Bambusa merrilliana): https://www.researchgate.net/publication/267029548_Physico-Mechanical_Properties_of_Culturally-Preformed_Bayog_Bambusa_merrilliana_Elmer_Rojo_Roxas_comb_nov

treatment_methods: Borax-boric acid (BBA) soak / vertical soak diffusion
description: Common, fast-growing, often non-straight culms — the most widely used bamboo overall, but very susceptible to powder-post beetle attack and therefore rarely used untreated as a primary building material. Best treated and used for secondary framing, walling, and scaffolding.

region: Native; common in Pangasinan, La Union, Ilocos Norte/Sur, Leyte, Panay, and Basilan
description: Thin-walled, small-diameter, native species used mainly for woven walling (sawali), roofing lath, plybamboo, and handicrafts rather than primary structure. Also processed into laminated buho lumber.
sources: FPRDI / RG — Development of laminated buho (Schizostachyum lumampao) lumber: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313057571_Development_of_laminated_buho_Schizostachyum_lumampao_Blanco_Merr_lumber
